definition: Desolate means deserted, dreary, and lifeless.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word desolate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know desolate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The moor above the tree line is desolate even in June — wind, peat, and a single fence post that lost its fence.
Empty is a fact about right now — the gym at six in the morning is empty and perfectly fine — while desolate stacks dreariness and lifelessness on top of the missing people.
Deserted goes further than empty — the people who belonged there have gone; desolate claims the most: emptied of life and cheer alike, with no sign anyone is coming back.

Bleak paints the outlook gray and unpromising — weather, moods, prospects. A bleak place can still be crowded and busy; the gloom is in what lies ahead. Desolate stacks real losses instead: the people, the cheer, and the life have already gone.

Forsaken means left behind by the people it needed — its keepers, its friends, its congregation. A forsaken place may still function; desolate goes all the way down: deserted and lifeless, with no sign of return.

The drought did what no historian could: it brought Harlow Bend back above the waterline for the first time since the valley was dammed in 1952.
Families who had grown up on stories of the place drove out to see it, and most fell quiet at the guardrail.
What the receding water revealed was desolate — a grid of gray mud streets, doorless doorframes, one church wall with its window a socket of silt.
